[[File:Cesare Montecucco 2011-01.JPG|thumb|Cesare Montecucco in Frankfurt in 2011, at the ceremony for the [[Paul Ehrlich and Ludwig Darmstaedter Prize]].]]

'''Cesare Montecucco''' (born 1 November 1947, in [[Trento]]) is an Italian pathologist and full professor at [[University of Padua]], [[Italy]]. He was awarded the [[Paul Ehrlich and Ludwig Darmstaedter Prize]] in 2011 for his research on [[tetanus]], [[botulism]], [[anthrax]] and ''[[Helicobacter pylori]]''-related diseases.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2010-10/guf-pcm102610.php|title=Professor Cesare Montecucco to receive the 2011 Paul Ehrlich and Ludwig Darmstaedter Prize|date=2010-10-26|website=EurekAlert!|publisher=|access-date=2016-11-01}}</ref>

Throughout his career, he was the recipient of many international awards in recognition for his research accomplishments in the fields of pathology, toxicology and immunology.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Montecucco |first=Cesare |date=2018-07-24 |title=An Interview with Cesare Montecucco |journal=Toxins |volume=10 |issue=8 |pages=307 |doi=10.3390/toxins10080307 |issn=2072-6651 |pmc=6116033 |pmid=30042331 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=FEMS Expert: Professor Cesare Montecucco |url=https://fems-microbiology.org/network/leading_opinion_in_science/eam-members/fems-expert-professor-cesar-montecucco/ |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=FEMS |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Cesare Montecucco, PhD |url=https://www.neurotoxins.org/board-of-directors/cesare-montecucco-phd/ |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=International Neurotoxin Association |language=en-US}}</ref>
